ops.title: FP appex ENOMEM launch storm — driven by 10s liveness probe, not per-item race
ops.body:
**Supersedes [[EDEADLK reading FP-synth settings.json — likely double-materialization race]] (note c8ad6679) as the primary explanation.** New evidence changed the picture: unified log showed fileproviderd failing to launch the CCPoolFileProvider appex with "Failed to consume sandbox extension ... errno=[12: Cannot allocate memory]" — 30,045 occurrences since 2026-07-13 23:45, still ongoing at time of writing (2026-07-14).

**Root cause of the churn (high confidence, code-traced)**: `internal/daemon/holder.go:67-89` (`healFuseRows`) runs `healTable` on a ticker every `defaultHealInterval` = 10 seconds (holder.go:19, registry.go:158-166). Every tick, `healFPRows` (internal/daemon/fpheal.go:238-275) calls `fpDomainProbe` (internal/overlay/fpprobe.go:84) → `RemoteDomainHost.ProbeDomain` (fusekit@v1.0.1 fileproviderd/remote.go:235-244) → the widget's control op → `probeDomain(_:)` in widget/Sources/App/FileProviderController.swift:401-433.

`probeDomain` is NOT the cheap zero-spawn stat its own doc comment claims. Every call does: (1) `mgr.getUserVisibleURL(for: .rootContainer)`, (2) a real `FileManager.contentsOfDirectory(atPath:)` readdir through the File Provider mount, (3) if `.claude.json` is listed, a real file open+read of the full byte count — deliberately never `stat()`, because "FPFS reports size 0 for materialized items" (their own comment). Steps 2-3 are genuine reads through the File Provider virtual filesystem, requiring fileproviderd to have the appex running. This runs unconditionally every 10s for every FP-backed account (healFPRows's only gates are `s.cl.held` and `fpDirLinked`; no backoff on the raw probe). The recovery ladder's backoff/breaker (fpRecoveryBackoff 30s→10m, fpRecoveryBreaker=5, `tripPark` — policies.go:52-56,143-149) only governs Teardown/Setup/bounce escalation AFTER a wedge verdict — it does NOT throttle the raw probe itself, so even a breaker-parked domain keeps hammering an appex launch attempt every 10s forever.

Rate check: 10s × N FP accounts over ~14h since 23:45 ≈ 30,240 at N≈6 accounts — matches the observed 30,045 almost exactly.

**(b) daemon push / pending-update fate**: zero Go call sites for Signal/signalEnumerator anywhere in cc-pool's daemon (confirmed by grep — only an unrelated os.Process.Signal in internal/cli/login.go). All FP working-set signaling is client-local in the widget: `signalAllDomains()` (FileProviderController.swift:558-576, the widget's own ~/.claude file watcher) and `rehydrate()` at app launch (:581-594). signalEnumerator is level-triggered, not a queue: a signal fired while the appex can't launch isn't lost, it just stays pending — fileproviderd re-diffs against on-disk truth whenever it next successfully runs. Meanwhile reads either serve stale cached bytes or fail outright (EDEADLK / ENOMEM-class) when a fresh materialization is needed and can't be serviced.

**Revised read on the original acct-13 EDEADLK**: very likely a symptom of this same appex-launch-failure condition racing a read, not primarily the per-item metadata/content coalescing gap described in c8ad6679. That gap is still real and worth closing eventually, but it's secondary to this probe design flaw.

**Fix directions** (not implemented):
1. Back off `probeDomain` per-domain once already wedged/parked instead of retrying at full 10s cadence forever.
2. Redesign the liveness probe to avoid a materializing read (e.g., tolerate the known FPFS size-0-on-stat quirk explicitly rather than substituting a full content read).
3. Separately: root-cause why the appex can't launch at all (ENOMEM) — a different question from what's hammering it.
